influences.name: His father (Jim McCartney)
influences.context: His father, a semi-professional musician, played a crucial role in introducing him to various genres, including: Music hall tunes, Broadway show songs, Jazz standards, Popular hits of the day

influences.name: George Martin
influences.context: McCartney's early production experiences were shaped by his work with George Martin during The Beatles era. This mentorship provided: Technical knowledge of recording processes, Understanding of arrangement and orchestration, Insights into the producer's role in shaping a song

influences.name: John Lennon
influences.context: The partnership between John Lennon and Paul McCartney was central to The Beatles' creative output. Their collaboration was characterized by: Shared musical influences and domain knowledge, Contrasting personalities that balanced each other, Ability to provide constructive criticism and feedback

influences.name: Geoffrey Chaucer
influences.context: He had a brilliant English literature teacher called Alan Durban. He got me to get interested [in writing] by telling me about The Miller's Tale [by Geoffrey Chaucer]. When I read it, I thought, 'This is great. It's really dirty.' And it gave me a lot of respect for Chaucer and then it got me interested in other bits of literature.

influences.name: William Shakespeare
influences.context: I did Hamlet and Henry V. At one point, I was thinking I'd love to direct a couple of plays. Hamlet was one.

influences.name: Allen Ginsberg
influences.context: I once worked with Allen Ginsberg and Allen always used to say, 'First thought, best thought.' And then he would edit everything. But I think the theory is good.
